name: Orzaqo
author: waheedev

sections.description:
Publishing a file once is not the same as being listed. Each AI shopping surface accepts products on its
own terms, and a product that satisfies one can be refused by another for a field the merchant never knew
mattered.

Orzaqo checks your catalog against those rules and keeps it republished as the catalog changes. Two
examples of what that means in practice: Google requires a brand on new products and refuses them without
one, while Perplexity keys product identity on GTIN — a product with no GTIN does not appear alongside the
same item from other stores at all. Orzaqo tells you which of your products each destination would
refuse, and why, before you find out from missing traffic.

The plugin’s job is delivery and evidence. It serves the artifacts Orzaqo generates — llms.txt,
robots.txt, sitemaps and your product feed — from your own domain rather than a third-party URL, and it
records which AI crawlers actually fetched them, so “are we being read?” has an answer rather than a
guess.

The plugin is thin by design: all publishing, structured-data generation, and analytics run on Orzaqo’s
servers and improve automatically, without a plugin update. The plugin only delivers those artifacts on
your domain and reports crawler activity — it stores no credentials beyond a single Orzaqo API key
obtained at connect time.

An Orzaqo account is required. The plugin delivers artifacts generated by the Orzaqo service and
cannot function without it. See “External Services” below for exactly what is sent and when.

External Services

This plugin connects to the Orzaqo API at https://api.orzaqo.com, operated by Orzaqo. The plugin is a
thin client: publishing, structured-data generation and analytics happen on Orzaqo’s servers, so the
plugin cannot function without that service. Nothing is sent before you connect a store.

What is sent, and when:

  • When you connect. The pairing code you paste and your store URL are sent to the Orzaqo API and
    exchanged for an API key. The plugin then creates a read-only WooCommerce REST key on your store and
    sends it to Orzaqo so your catalog can be pulled.
  • When your catalog syncs. Orzaqo pulls product data through that read-only key: titles,
    descriptions, prices, stock status, images, categories, brands and product identifiers such as GTIN.
    Only published products are read. When a product changes or is deleted, its product id is sent so the
    change is picked up.
  • About once an hour. The plugin fetches the list of files to serve and reports how many products the
    store publishes.
  • When an AI crawler or a shopper requests an artifact. Requests to paths such as /llms.txt,
    /robots.txt, sitemaps and the product feed are proxied to the Orzaqo API, which renders them, so
    they are served on your own domain.
  • When an AI crawler visits your store. Its user agent, the path it requested and, on a product page,
    the product id. No IP address is sent.
  • When a visitor arrives from an AI assistant. The referring site’s host name (for example
    chatgpt.com) and the page they landed on.
  • When a shopper uses your store’s search. The words they searched for, so unanswered demand can be
    reported to you. Orzaqo removes email addresses, phone numbers and long digit runs before storing them.
  • When a product page is viewed. Its structured data (JSON-LD) is fetched from Orzaqo and cached on
    your site.
  • When an order follows an Orzaqo assistant recommendation. The order number, the order total, the
    total of the recommended item and the currency, so the sale can be attributed. No customer name,
    address, email or payment detail is ever sent.
  • In your shoppers’ browsers. If the storefront assistant is enabled for your plan, its script is
    loaded from https://api.orzaqo.com, and the questions shoppers type into it are sent to Orzaqo to be
    answered from your catalog. It sets no cookies; the conversation is kept in the browser tab’s
    session storage and is gone when the tab closes.

What is stored on your site: the Orzaqo API key, your merchant id and name, the API base, the served
route list, the widget key and its appearance settings, your plan’s limits and usage, the id of the
WooCommerce key it created, and short queues of events waiting to be sent. On orders that followed an
assistant recommendation it stores an Orzaqo reference and the time it was reported; until checkout, that
reference is kept in the shopper’s WooCommerce session. Uninstalling deletes every setting and queue; cached
copies of served files expire within five minutes; the order references stay with those orders.

Terms of Service: https://orzaqo.com/terms
Privacy Policy: https://orzaqo.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Settings -> Orzaqo.
  3. Paste the pairing code from your Orzaqo dashboard and click Connect.

To point the plugin at a non-production Orzaqo API (e.g. local development), define
ORZAQO_API_BASE in your wp-config.php.
sections.faq:
Do I need an Orzaqo account?

Yes. The plugin delivers artifacts that Orzaqo generates, so it needs an account to pair with. You paste
a pairing code from the Orzaqo dashboard; the plugin does the rest.

What data leaves my store?

Product data; your store URL; AI crawler visits (user agent and path, never an IP address); the host name
of AI assistants that send you visitors; the words shoppers search for on your store; and, for orders that
followed an assistant recommendation, the order number and totals. No customer names, addresses, emails or
payment details. See “External Services” above for when each is sent.

Does it slow my store down?

Publishing and analysis run on Orzaqo’s servers, not yours. On storefront pages the plugin adds the
assistant’s script if your plan includes it, and product pages fetch their structured data from Orzaqo
when it is not already cached (with a 5-second limit). Crawler and search reports are queued and sent in
batches.

What happens when I uninstall it?

Every setting and queue the plugin stored is deleted, and its cached copies expire within five minutes.
Order references added to attributed orders stay with those orders. The read-only WooCommerce key it created is revoked when you disconnect.

Can I point it at a different Orzaqo environment?

Yes. Define ORZAQO_API_BASE in wp-config.php and it takes precedence over everything else. This is
also how a store behind split-horizon DNS reaches the API on an internal hostname.
sections.changelog:
0.1.5

  • Readme: “External Services” now lists everything the plugin sends and stores, including attributed-order totals, on-site search text and the storefront assistant script.
  • Uninstalling now removes every setting, queue and cache the plugin creates.
  • Crawler detection recognises Claude-SearchBot.

0.1.4

  • Settings: the Orzaqo screen now tells you when a new version is available, with a link to WordPress’s own updater.
  • Settings: one click turns on WordPress automatic updates for Orzaqo, so fixes reach your store as soon as they ship. You can turn it off on the Plugins screen.

0.1.3

  • robots.txt: Orzaqo now adds its sitemap to your existing robots.txt instead of replacing it. Rules from WordPress, WooCommerce and SEO plugins such as Yoast are kept.
  • robots.txt: nothing is added when your site is set to discourage search engines.
  • robots.txt: the sitemap reference now points at your own domain.

0.1.2

  • The settings screen now links to your Orzaqo account, and to account creation if you do not have one. It previously asked for a pairing code without saying where to get one.

0.1.1

  • The assistant now paints your own colour on its first frame instead of briefly showing a default one.
  • Only published products are read, as this page has always said — drafts are no longer requested.
  • Artifact responses carry an explicit content type chosen by the plugin, and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
  • Orzaqo’s own requests identify themselves, so they are no longer counted as crawler traffic on your store.

0.1.0

  • Initial release: one-click connect (pairing code), on-domain artifact delivery, and AI-crawler sensing.
